plan_a_advantages: A more balanced approach to building endurance and speed, with a focus on maintaining freshness between sessions.
Includes a dedicated long run on varied terrain, crucial for trail running.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates a dedicated interval session for developing higher-end aerobic power.
Includes a strength and mobility session, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall performance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent, moderate-intensity running and incorporates varied terrain, directly addressing the demands of trail running. Plan B, while including interval training, focuses heavily on building aerobic capacity with longer, easier runs and a dedicated strength session, which might not be the most efficient way to improve speed for a runner already with a base level of fitness. Plan A’s structure feels more targeted towards developing the specific adaptations needed for trail speed, while Plan B feels more generalized.
